rubric.written: 2026-10-17. The rules were written down while the list of places was being read for the first time, one rule as each case first arrived; the class of each place was then written to this file after the whole list had been read. The rubric was not fixed before any place was seen. The sample is drawn from this file, so it came after the classification. The classification uses only the string the specialist wrote (name and locality) and general knowledge; it never uses a web lookup, because whether the place is real is what the sample measures.

named-premises.definition: A proper name that picks out one establishment, site or attraction: something with a door, a gate or a visit. Includes a named natural feature visited as an attraction (a rock, a mountain, a lake, a cape), a named square, a trail or wharf with its own name, and a national park when the candidate is a visit.
named-premises.example: Exploramer; Musée de la Gaspésie; Roscioli; Hotel Raphael; Percé Rock

kind-of-place.definition: A category at a locality, or a description that does not name its object: nothing in the string tells two premises of that kind apart. Includes a placeholder ('to be chosen', 'specific property not yet chosen', 'e.g.'), a plural ('motels'), an either/or, a tour or service, an organisation or an online service, and a branded accommodation type.
kind-of-place.example: Motel in Percé; Local cheese producer; Resort kids' club (resort not named)

settlement-or-area.definition: A town, village, region, island or district as an area, a neighbourhood, or a national park named as the region a route passes through (a `between` endpoint). Whatever specialist proposed it and whether it is used as a stop, a settlement is this class.
settlement-or-area.example: Percé; Prati district; Gaspésie; Québec City

route-or-transit.definition: A road, a crossing, or a node on a movement: a station, a terminal, an airport, a bus stop, a trailhead, a ferry or boat departure point, a park entrance or gateway.
route-or-transit.example: Wien Hauptbahnhof; Rivière-du-Loup ferry terminal; Mont-Albert trailhead

edgeRules.park-visit: A national park is named-premises when it is proposed as a visit (an `at` location, or any occurrence of the key that is an `at`), including a named sector of it. One key that is a `between` endpoint in some records and an `at` in others takes named-premises.
edgeRules.park-area: A national park is settlement-or-area when the only use of the key is as an endpoint of a `between`, a region a route passes through.
edgeRules.established-descriptive-name: A string built from a locality and a category is named-premises only when it is the established name of one landmark that a reader would know without a map (Ljubljana Castle, Percé Rock, Cap-des-Rosiers lighthouse, the English form of Phare de Cap-des-Rosiers). This is judged from general knowledge, not a lookup.
edgeRules.locality-plus-category: Every other string built from a locality and a singular category (Gaspé aquarium, Percé wharf, Camping de Carleton-sur-Mer) is kind-of-place even when only one such object plausibly exists, because the string does not name it. These are the rows most likely to move to named-premises under a looser reading; the Log gives the count with and without them.
edgeRules.natural-feature: A named natural feature visited as an attraction (mountain, lake, ridge, cape, plateau) is named-premises: it is a site with a visit.
edgeRules.two-sites: A string naming two sites joined by 'and', '/' or a comma is named-premises when each half would be, and counts once.
edgeRules.square: A named piazza or square is named-premises: a site, not a district.
edgeRules.landmark-as-route-stop: A landmark used as a `between` endpoint keeps its own class (named-premises); only settlements and parks-as-regions change class by use.
edgeRules.transit-node: Airports, stations, terminals, bus stops, trailheads, boat or ferry departure points, park entrances and gateways are route-or-transit, even when they carry a proper name, because the candidate is a stop on a movement.
edgeRules.branded-category: A product or brand name for a kind of accommodation at a park (oTENTik) names a type, not one premises: kind-of-place.
edgeRules.placeholder: A string that says in its own words that the premises is not chosen is kind-of-place whatever else it names.
